why: Every expected word and bound is derived by hand from the WGSL pack/unpack definitions: pack4x8unorm and pack2x16unorm round half up (floor(0.5 + max*value)), the emissive code is RGBM over 128, the radiance code is square-root over 512 and the octahedral code is signed snorm. No value comes from a GPU run or from the code under test.

emissive.why: encode_emissive: peak = clamp(max(e)/128, 1e-6, 1); scale = ceil(255*peak)/255; d = 128*scale; each colour byte is floor(0.5 + 255*e/d) and the alpha byte is floor(0.5 + 255*scale). decode multiplies byte/255 by scale*128, so one byte of quantisation is d/255 and a round trip stays within that one step.

round_trips.why: zero encodes with the 1e-6 peak floor to a zero colour and decodes back to exactly zero
128 is the exact peak: scale 1 and a red byte of 255
peak 40/128 gives scale 80/255 and d = 10240/255 = 40.1569, so one step is d/255 = 0.15748

packed.why: scale 1, d 128: red floor(0.5+255)=255, green floor(0.5+127.5)=128, blue 0, alpha 255, low byte first, so 0xFF0080FF

radiance.why: encode_radiance: e = sqrt(clamp(c/512, 0, 1)); each half is floor(0.5 + 65535*e) with x in the low half. A half-step in e maps to at most 512*(0.5/65535)*(2e + 0.5/65535) in c, which is the bound used for a round trip.

round_trips.why: zero encodes to two zero words and decodes back to zero
at the 512 range the square-root code is 1, so both words pack as all ones
2, 8 and 32 have exact roots 0.0625, 0.125 and 0.25, so the round trip only sees the 16-bit half-step

exact.why: both square-root components are 1: pack2x16unorm(1,1)=0xFFFFFFFF and pack2x16unorm(1,0)=0x0000FFFF

oct.why: oct_encode divides by the L1 norm, folds the negative-z hemisphere and packs with pack2x16snorm (floor(0.5 + 32767*value)); oct_decode unfolds and normalises. The decoded direction is compared with the normalised input, not with the raw input.

cases.why: +x: s=1, p=(1,0), e=(1,0) packs as (32767, 0) and decodes back to +x
-y: p=(0,-1) packs as (0,-32767) and decodes back to -y
+z: p=(0,0) packs to the zero word and decodes back to +z
(1,1,1)/sqrt(3) has p=(1/3,1/3); 16-bit snorm quantisation keeps the decoded direction within 1e-3
